Lung and chest wall statics

Change the compliance of the lung or the chest wall and watch the relaxation curves, FRC, TLC, and RV move. The lungs want to be small, the chest wall wants to be big, and FRC is where the two pulls balance.

Sets how far muscles can push the system toward TLC and RV

Compliance multipliers divide the recoil pressure at every volume. The lung curve pivots on its collapsed volume. The chest wall curve pivots near RV, so a stiffer chest wall also has a smaller resting volume.

THINK THROUGH THE RESPONSE

Where do the pulls balance?

At FRC the lung recoils inward and the chest wall recoils outward with equal and opposite pressures. Which way should FRC move if the lung becomes stiffer?

HOW THE CURVES COMBINE

Same volume, pressures add

The lung and chest wall are coupled by the pleural space, so they always have the same volume (except in pneumothorax). To hold the relaxed system at any volume, you need the pressure that holds the lung there plus the pressure that holds the chest wall there:

Prs(V) = PL(V) + Pcw(V)

So the combined curve is built by adding the two curves horizontally, along the pressure axis, at each volume. Take the slope of both sides:

1 / Crs = 1 / CL + 1 / Ccw

That is the rule for compliances in series, like two springs hooked end to end. The combined system is always stiffer than either part. Compare the vascular compliances in the circulation, which sit side by side at the same pressure and add directly (Ctotal = C1 + C2). Adding the lung and chest wall volumes at the same pressure would be the parallel rule, and it gives the wrong curve.

Model details. Lung: V = Vmax − (Vmax − V0)·e−kP (Salazar–Knowles exponential), V0 1.5 L, Vmax 6.4 L. Chest wall: logistic curve with a resting volume of 4.0 L; compliance changes pivot it at 1.5 L. Compliance is read as the slope at FRC, so it can differ from the slider multiplier when FRC moves along a curved line. Healthy values: FRC 3.0 L, TLC 6.0 L, RV 1.5 L, CL 0.25, Ccw 0.18, Crs 0.10 L/cmH₂O. TLC and RV are where maximal inspiratory and expiratory muscle effort balance the system's recoil. RV here is set by the chest wall, as in young adults. Airway closure, which raises RV with age and in emphysema, depends on flow and will come with the PFT module.
